review_type: offline character-device removal and in-flight I/O lifetime review

evidence.observation: Loads tcm_hcd through g_cdev_data before acquiring qword_316A0, then holds qword_316A0 around the raw read.
Loads tcm_hcd through g_cdev_data before acquiring qword_316A0, then holds qword_316A0 around the raw write.

Uses qword_316D0 for the client-list teardown, calls cdev_del, warns if qword_31698 is nonzero, frees qword_31658 through devm_kfree, resets shared state, and finally sets g_cdev_data to zero. It does not acquire qword_316A0 or qword_31668 before freeing the I/O state.
The raw-read path increments the shared reference counter and reads, allocates, clears, and uses qword_31658 as its transfer buffer.
The raw-write path increments the shared reference counter and reads, allocates, clears, and uses qword_31658 as its transfer buffer.
Calls syna_cdev_remove before disconnecting the TCM device and releasing additional managed and heap allocations.

findings.kernel_api_contract: Linux 6.12 cdev_del prevents new opens, but already-open descriptors retain callable file_operations after cdev_del returns.
race_scenarios: An already-open descriptor invokes read/write after cdev_del; the fop still runs and dereferences g_cdev_data before any null or shutdown check. If removal has set g_cdev_data to zero, the access through g_cdev_data + 168 is invalid.

A read/write already inside the raw operation holds qword_316A0 and uses qword_31658. Removal does not acquire qword_316A0 or qword_31668; it only logs a nonzero qword_31698 reference count and continues to free qword_31658 and clear the shared state.
findings.runtime_assessment: The cdev API contract and lock/free ordering establish a reachable static race for open descriptors. The existing host harnesses are sequential stub-based tests; they do not model concurrent file descriptors, kernel cdev lifetime, or a live managed allocation. Runtime reproduction has not been performed.

stock_comparison.existing_evidence: Each function has existing canonical Docker and host-harness evidence; read/write/remove microtask attestations report two canonical build cycles.

findings.reconstruction_decision: Keep the reconstructed functions stock-exact and record this as a separate hardening deviation. A safe fix needs a shutdown state and a lifetime protocol for already-open descriptors, with all operations acquiring a valid object reference before dereferencing state; then drain in-flight I/O before freeing the shared buffer and TCM context.

findings.review: The qword_316D0 lock protects removal of the report/client list, whose enqueue/dequeue paths also use qword_316D0. That explains the list kfree calls. This lock does not protect the separate raw-I/O state, which uses qword_316A0/qword_31668; the first finding records that independent lifetime race.
